title: From Self-Taught Beginner to Steam: How Would You Approach This?
author: Embarrassed-Ad-4740
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I'm starting to get into game development as a completely self-taught beginner, and I'm trying to understand both the technical side and the overall process of creating and publishing a game.

My long-term goal is to release a game on **Steam**, but right now I have very little idea about all the steps required to get there. How would you approach it if you were starting today?

The game I'm trying to build is a mix of a **management game**, **RimWorld**, and a **city builder**, focused on resource management, progression, and base/city development.

I'd love to get some advice from people with more experience:

* What would be the main development steps you'd follow for a project like this?
* Which game engine and software would you recommend today?
* Would you start with a very small prototype first, or jump directly into building the full game?
* What are the biggest mistakes beginners should avoid?

To be completely honest, I'm not a professional programmer. I'm trying to build everything with the help of modern AI tools, which can often help me tackle problems I wouldn't even know how to approach on my own.

At the moment, I'm mainly using **Codex** and **Claude Code** to assist with development, and they've been incredibly helpful so far.

Any advice, personal experiences, recommended resources, or reality checks would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks! 🚀🎮

comments.author: korypostma
comments.body:
I'll summarize what could be a very long book into a few things:
1. Use the 90/10 engineering principal.  Do 90% of the work with 10% effort.  Save that last 10% of the work for when you have 90% effort available.  This is like saying prototype first, polish later.
2. Godot with GDExtensions, I have used UE4/UE5 and Unity, as well, in the past.
3. Full game prototype, make sure it is fun.  Let people close to you play it, they won't always be honest to not hurt your feelings.  Find unbiased people online to test it and provide constructive feedback.
4. Beginners waste too much time on details that don't matter right now.  Focus on the code and gameplay loop, polish comes later.  Plan first before implementing.
